notes:
Inbound SMB lead — self-serve signup, small support biz handling chat tickets. Primary goal: replace current hosted LLM vendor for automated triage + suggested replies. Using hosted_api; running on public cloud. Current POC: streaming responses with function-calling to populate structured ticket fields (priority, category, root_cause). Typical model: open-chat-medium-v1 (customer named), temperature low. Problems reported: 
- When using streaming mode + function schema, about 15% of responses arrive with trailing fragments or wrap-around that breaks customer's JSON.parse step. Example failure (copied from logs): 
  --- snippet ---
  data: {"delta": "{\"priority\": \"high\", \"category\": \"login\", \"root\": \"password reset required\""}
  data: [DONE]
  --- end ---
  The customer parses line-delimited JSON and sometimes gets partial objects because the stream chunk boundary happens in middle of JSON object; their current handler rejects partial objects instead of buffering.
- Function schema mismatch: customer schema field 'root_cause' vs model returning 'root' or nested arrays. On call they use function_metadata v1 with schema required properties; model output occasionally omits required props and Redwoods' fallback policy returns text chunk instead of function call. They see error: "function output does not conform to schema" in their validation layer.
- SDK integration: they are using an older HTTP streaming client; asked for recommended Node streaming snippet and whether Redwood's streaming guarantees chunk alignment for JSON mode.
Customer comments: "We need reliable structured output — our webhook consumer cannot accept malformed JSON; otherwise we'll have to post-process which defeats automation."  
Notes from SE: likely causes - 1) client-side stream handling not buffering across 'data:' events; 2) model may emit non-standard keys when guidance is weak; 3) call settings (stop tokens, max_tokens, chunking) need adjustment. Suggested mitigations discussed: enforce function_call in request, supply strict JSON schema with examples, enable Redwood structured_output mode, add per-chunk buffering and assembly in handler, and optionally set response_format: json-mode-strict if available.
Open ask: provide a minimal reproducible curl + Node streaming example that demonstrates buffering and function schema enforcement. Also confirm whether Redwood will return a single function invocation token at end of stream or stream the full JSON in chunks (we should document expected behavior).
